behavior: Reviewer adapter admission is serialized by canonical product across processes using the existing OS file-lock helper; different products are independent.
Queued cancellation and an already-cancelled pre-start context prevent adapter launch. Queue errors retain their stage and wrapped context error.
A nonzero adapter error remains wrapped and carries a fixed safe category recognized from real native learning reviewer diagnostics.
Arbitrary stderr, paths, provider messages and credentials are never copied to the durable RV; unknown details are explicitly withheld.
The common duplicate-start job guard, shared module version and verified-use semantics are unchanged.

verification.skip_details: Three helper entrypoints are skipped outside their subprocess modes. The dangling-symlink fixture was skipped because the host lacks the required symlink privilege.
direct_proofs: Two helper processes cannot enter one product's reviewer slot together; a different product can enter.
Configured Reviewer callback returns on queued cancellation without launching its adapter.
Production adapter invalid-model-output, duplicate-job, private-error and no-candidate paths persist linked event_id/run_id/review_id and expected RV outcomes.
Wrapped exit status, protocol failure and timeout remain distinguishable.

independent_review.launcher: Codex CLI through AIR Commander Test

evidence: HEAD matches the requested SHA; review covered the committed diff and its direct adapter, lock, and saved-RV paths.

The reviewer callback locks the opened product’s canonical path, checks context while queued and after acquisition, and releases the lock after the adapter returns. The pre-start context check prevents an already-cancelled launch.

Production adapter errors use the reviewed stderr format. Nonzero exit errors remain wrapped; only fixed categories, never raw stderr, reach the module’s durable RV. The tests invoke the native command and printer with only provider output stubbed, then check RV linkage and outcomes.
Coordinator reports 76 passes, 4 skips, no failures, plus successful vet, build, and diff check on the same bytes.
limitations: Tests were not rerun in this read-only review; POSIX execution was not tested.
This review does not close the canonical PLAN or prove production learning or autonomy. Running-process recovery, legacy .out archival, and skill delivery and useful use remain outside scope.
